messages.subject: Detected use of non-constant indexes
parts:
Hi all,

I hope your week is going well.

I encountered the following error message when fitting a mixture model:
Defining model [Note] Detected use of non-constant indexes: z[2], z[3], z[4], z[5], z[6], z[7], z[8], z[9], z[10], z[11], z[12], z[13], z[14], z[15], z[16], z[17], z[18], z[19], z[20], z[21], z[22], z[23], z[24], z[25], z[26], z[27], z[28], z[29], z[30], z[31], z[32], z[33], z[34], z[35], z[36], z[37], z[38], z[39], z[40], z[41], z[42], z[43], z[44], z[45], z[46], z[47], z[48], z[49], z[50], ... For computational efficiency we recommend specifying these in 'constants'. Building model Setting data and initial values Running calculate on model [Note] Any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables. Error in model$modelDef$declInfo[[declID]] : attempt to select less than one element in integerOneIndex
Checking model sizes and dimensions Error in nimble::getParam(.self, node, param): getParam only works for one node at a time, but z[] includes multiple nodes.

The nimble function and model are as follows:
piFun <- nimbleFunction(
run = function(r = double(1)) {
rlength <- length(r)
rsum <- rep(0, rlength)
pi <- rep(0, rlength)
rsum[1] <- pi[1] <- r[1]
for (i in 2:rlength) {
rsum[i] <- rsum[i - 1] + r[i]
if (rsum[i] >= 1) {
pi[i] <- 1 - rsum[i - 1]
}
else {pi[i] <- r[i]}
}
for (i in 1:rlength) {
if (pi[i] < 0) {pi[i] <- 0}
}
returnType(double(1))
return(pi)
})

gmm_mfm_W <- nimbleCode({
#===========================
# likelihood specification
#===========================
z[i] ~ dcat(pi[1:M])
for(i in 1:N){
for(t in 1:Time){
y[i,t] ~ dnorm(muy[i,t], var = sig2[t])
muy[i,t] <- LS[i,1] + ss[t]*LS[i,2]
}
LS[i,1:2] ~ dmnorm(muLS[z[i],1:2], cov=Cov_b[1:2,1:2])
}
#===========================
# prior specification
#===========================
# --------- SBP ---------
# --------- pi ---------
for (m in 1:M) {
r_beta[m] ~ dexp(rate = lambda_beta)
}
pi[1:M] <- piFun(r = r_beta[1:M])
lambda_beta ~ dlnorm(0, varlog = 1)
# --------- muLS ---------
for (m in 1:M) {
muLS[m,1] ~ dnorm(0, var = 100) # Intercept
muLS[m,2] ~ dnorm(0, var = 100) # Slope
}
# --------- Cov_b ---------
Cov_b[1:2,1:2] ~ dinvwish(R[1:2,1:2],2)
R[1,1] <- 1
R[2,2] <- 1
R[2,1] <- R[1,2]
R[1,2] <- 0
# --------- sig2 ---------
for(t in 1:Time) {
sig2[t] ~ dinvgamma(1, 1)
}
})

# Run the MCMC
Time <- 4
M <- 10
nmcmc <- 10000
nburn <- 5000
nthin <- 1
consts <- list(N=N, Time=Time, ss=0:(Time-1), M=M)
inits <- list(pi=rep(0.1,M), lambda_beta=1, r_beta=rep(0.2,M),
              muLS=matrix(rep(c(6,0.5),each=N),nrow=N), sig2=rep(0.5,Time),
              z=sample(1:5, size=N, replace=TRUE), Cov_b=diag(2))
dat <- list(y=dat.K3)
model <- nimbleModel(gmm_mfm_W, data=dat, inits=inits, constants=consts) 
cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors=c('z'), print=TRUE)
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project=model)
samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc, niter=nmcmc, nburnin=0, thin=1, setSeed=TRUE)

This error message looks quite scary, and I am not able to fix it. However, I was surprised to find that the MCMC worked normally. 

I would appreciate your help a lot. Thank you very much.


Best,
Meng
